$comment: What the vector index answers after what it was told, as every implementation of the index must answer: a history of writes, and what each read then gives. Semiont's stores (semiont_vectors, packages/vectors-python) run every case: the in-memory store, and the Qdrant store against a real Qdrant. What a point is, and how each store keys one, is specs/src/vectors/payload-cases.json. A HISTORY. `writes` are done in order, on an index that holds nothing and states no stamp. `resourcePut` gives a resource's `chunks` (each an `index`, a `text` and an `embedding`), the `contentChecksum` of the bytes they came from, the `mediaType` those bytes were read as, its `entityTypes`, and `machineRead` when the text was read from pixels: the resource's points become these, every point it had before is gone, and so is whatever the index remembered of a decline of it. `entityTypesRewritten` sets the entity types on every point of a resource's chunks and changes nothing else, and `annotationEntityTypesRewritten` sets them on the one point of the annotation `annotationId` and changes nothing else: neither makes a point where there is none. `annotationPut` gives an annotation's one point: its `annotationId`, `resourceId`, `motivation` and `entityTypes`, the `text` it quotes and that text's `embedding`, and `machineRead` when that text was read from pixels. `resourceDeleted` takes every point of a resource's chunks, and whatever the index remembered of a decline of it; `annotationDeleted` takes an annotation's point, and `annotationsOfResourceDeleted` takes the point of every annotation on a resource. `resourceDeclined` is of a resource whose bytes gave no text to index: it takes every point of the resource's chunks, and has the index remember in their place the `contentChecksum` of those bytes, the `mediaType` they were read as and the `reason`, each as it is given. A resource has points or is remembered so, and never both; one declined again is remembered as it was last declined; and the points of annotations on it are touched by none of this. `madeAnew` takes everything out of the index, every point of both collections and everything remembered of a decline, and has the index state the `stamp` given: what made its points, as whoever writes the index says it, which the index keeps whole and reads nothing of. READS. `reads` are made after the writes, in order, and none of them changes anything; each states what it `answers`. `resourcesSearched` and `annotationsSearched` search one collection by an `embedding`, and `searchedByResource` searches the resources by the vectors the chunks of the resource `resourceId` have. Each answers a list of results, best first. A result is a `score`, the `resourceId`, the `annotationId` of an annotation's point, the `text`, the `entityTypes`, and `machineRead` where the point is marked; its `id` is each store's own key and is not stated. A search of resources by an embedding answers one result for each chunk: a resource found by three of its chunks is three results. A search by a resource's own vectors answers one result for each resource, with the score and the text of the chunk of it that scored best against any chunk of the resource searched by, and never answers that resource itself. `counted` answers the number of points in both collections together: what is remembered of a decline is no point, and is not counted. `stampsListed` answers the stamp of every resource that has points, by its id: the `contentChecksum`, the `mediaType`, the `entityTypes`, and `machineRead` where its points are marked. `stampRead` answers the stamp of the one resource `resourceId`, and has no `answers` where that resource has no points. `annotationStampsListed` answers the stamp of every annotation that has a point, by its id: the `resourceId` its point says it is on, and the `entityTypes` its point carries, in their order. `declinedListed` answers what the index remembers of every declined resource, by its id: the `contentChecksum`, the `mediaType` and the `reason`. `indexStampRead` answers the stamp the index states, and has no `answers` where it states none: nothing has made it anew. The stamps listed, of resources and of annotations, and the declined listed are sets: no order of theirs is stated. A SEARCH takes a `limit`, the most results it answers, and may take a `scoreThreshold` and a `filter`. A score is the cosine of the angle between two vectors, whatever their lengths: 1 when they point the same way, 0 at a right angle, -1 when they point opposite ways. Scores are stated to six decimal places and compared within 0.000001. With a threshold, a point that scores below it is not answered. A point is answered only if every member of the filter holds of it. `entityTypes` keeps a point that has any one of the types listed, and `excludeEntityTypes` drops a point that has any one of them; an empty list of either filters nothing. `resourceId` keeps the points of that resource alone, and `excludeResourceId` drops them. `motivation` keeps the annotations of that motivation alone. The limit counts what the filter and the threshold leave. WHAT NO CASE RESTS ON. No two results of one read have the same score, so no case says how a tie is broken. No score equals its threshold: the in-memory store answers such a point, and whether Qdrant does is Qdrant's to say. No limit is 0, about which the two stores disagree. Every search by a resource's own vectors has a limit well above the number of points there are, and finds resources of one or two chunks: with more, Qdrant's store can miss a resource the in-memory store finds. No stamp of an index has a null in it: whether a Qdrant keeps one is Qdrant's to say. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: an index nothing was written to answers nothing: no result, no stamp, no annotation, nothing remembered of a decline, and a count of 0. Nothing has made it anew, so it states no stamp of its own

a search of resources by an embedding answers one result for each chunk and not one for each resource, best first; a search of annotations answers annotations' points alone; and the count is of the points of both

putting a resource's vectors replaces all it had: a resource that shrinks from three chunks to one keeps no point of the three, its stamp is the new one, the mark of the old text is gone, and another resource's points are as they were

chunks.text: the first old chunk of a
the second old chunk of a
the third old chunk of a

cases.why: putting no chunks leaves a resource with no points, and so with no stamp: the checksum and the entity types given with no chunk are kept nowhere
putting an annotation's vector again replaces its one point, the vector and all of the payload: what it was first put with is found by nothing

rewriting a resource's entity types changes them on every one of its points, and so its stamp and what a filter finds. The checksum, the mark, the texts and the vectors are as they were, and so are another resource's points and the resource's annotations, which keep the entity types they were put with
rewriting the entity types of a resource that has no points does nothing: no point is made, and the resource has no stamp

rewriting an annotation's entity types changes them on its one point, in the order given, and so what the listing answers of it and what a filter finds. The resource it is on, its motivation, the mark, the text and the vector are as they were, and so are the points of its resource and of every other annotation, which keep the entity types they were put with
rewriting the entity types of an annotation that has no point is no failure and does nothing: no point is made, and the points there are keep the entity types they were put with
deleting a resource's vectors takes every point of its chunks and nothing else: another resource's points stay, and so does every annotation's point, those of annotations on the deleted resource too
deleting an annotation's vector takes that one point: the other annotations on its resource stay, and so do the resource's own points
deleting a resource's annotations' vectors takes the point of every annotation on that resource, and leaves the resource's own points and the annotations on other resources
deleting what is not there is no failure, and changes nothing
a filter by entity types keeps a point that has any one of them, and not only a point that has them all; a point with no entity types is never kept by it
a filter that leaves entity types out drops a point that has any one of them, and keeps a point that has none
an empty list of entity types filters nothing, whether it is of types to keep or of types to leave out: every point is answered
a filter by resource keeps the points of that resource alone, in a search of either collection
a filter that leaves a resource out drops every point of that resource, in a search of either collection
a filter by motivation keeps the annotations of that motivation alone
the members of a filter must all hold: a point is answered when it passes every one of them, and a point that passes one and fails another is not
a score threshold drops every point that scores below it
the limit keeps the best: of five points, the two that score highest, best first
the limit counts what the filter left: the best two of the points that pass, and not what passes of the best two
with no threshold a search answers every point up to its limit, however poorly it scores, best first: a point at a right angle scores 0, and one that points the opposite way scores -1
a search by a resource's own vectors answers the other resources nearest to them, best first: the resource itself is left out, and no annotation's point is searched

a search by a resource's own vectors is cut to its limit in resources, and not in chunks: a resource with many chunks near the one searched by takes one place of the answer, and the next resource is answered though nine chunks of the first are nearer than its one

a search by a resource's own vectors answers one result for each resource: a resource found by two of its chunks is answered once, with the score and the text of the chunk that scored best. A search of resources by an embedding answers both chunks

a search by a resource's own vectors drops a resource whose best chunk scores below the threshold

The point of an annotation on it is as it was, and so are another resource's points
